outcome: The legacy virtual firewall is replaced in place by a modern next-generation platform without redesigning the surrounding network.
overview: Replacing a virtual firewall that still works is a hard case to make until it stops receiving updates, and then it becomes urgent. An IT services enterprise in the region migrated its existing virtual firewall to FortiGate — a straightforward next-generation replacement, delivered as a migration rather than a redesign. Engagements like this one are worth doing precisely because they are unglamorous: the common case is not a transformation programme, it is a supported platform reaching its end of life and a rule base that has to move without breaking anything.

benefits.text: A next-generation platform replaces a legacy virtual firewall without redesigning the network
benefits.limits: The published reference describes one named customer engagement. It is evidence that Redington has delivered this, and it is not a performance figure that transfers to the next customer

benefits.text: Application-aware policy replaces port-and-protocol rules inherited from the previous platform
benefits.limits: Only where rules are actually rewritten; a like-for-like conversion carries the port-based posture across and delivers a new platform with the old policy

benefits.text: The same policy model extends to virtual and cloud form factors as the estate moves
benefits.limits: The same operating system runs on the appliance, as a virtual machine and in cloud, so the capability claim survives a form-factor change; the throughput figure behind it does not, and must be re-sized per form factor

residency: Virtual appliances run inside the customer’s own virtualisation or cloud tenancy; policy and logs stay within the estate

notFor.situation: A firewall platform still fully supported with a current rule base
notFor.why: Replacement without an end-of-support or capability driver is change for its own sake

notFor.situation: An estate needing a segmentation redesign rather than a platform swap
notFor.why: A migration preserves the design; if the design is the problem, migrating it preserves the problem

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Fortinet implementation partner · Duration: 4–8 weeks depending on rule-base size and window availability
Support model: Vendor subscription support; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed policy operations with a quarterly rule review.
1) Analyse — rule export, shadowed and permissive rule identification, throughput measurement
2) Convert — rules rewritten in application terms with the exceptions listed explicitly
3) Rehearse — cutover runbook validated with a rollback path to the incumbent
4) Cut over and hand over — migration executed in window, operations handed over
deliverables: The measured share of rules expressed as application policy meets the figure agreed at design
Rules with no application equivalent are listed explicitly rather than left implicit
Rollback to the incumbent is demonstrated during rehearsal, not merely documented
effort: 4–8 weeks depending on rule-base size and window availability
